title: A 16-second teaser plan
scenario:
A running-shoe brand wants a vertical 16-second teaser. You plan two 8-second shots with a video model that makes sound with the picture and accepts up to three reference images of the product.

Your first draft prompt is in the exhibit. The first test clip was a blur of cuts, with no clear shoe and no sound that fits.
exhibit:
Draft prompt (one request)
  "Cool teaser for our new sneaker: a runner sprints through the city,
   then we see the laces close up, then a drone shot over rooftops,
   then the logo appears. Epic feel."

Prompt elements the vendor's guide lists
  subject, action, style, camera positioning and motion (optional),
  composition (optional), focus and lens effects (optional), ambiance (optional)

Audio cues the vendor's guide lists
  dialogue: use quotes for specific speech
  sound effects: describe them
  ambient noise: describe the soundscape

Client asks
  - One line spoken by the runner at the end: Run your city.
  - Same white sneaker with a green heel tab in both shots.

questions.prompt: What is the main problem with the draft prompt?

options.text: It runs four shots together in one sentence. Each shot needs its own prompt or shot block, with one action.
options.explanation: Right. Runway's tips say "Write one clear idea per shot", and OpenAI's Sora 2 guide says to keep each shot block distinct: one camera setup, one subject action and one lighting recipe.

options.text: It is too short. Longer prompts always work better, so add more adjectives and words. Add more about the street and shoe.
options.explanation: Length is not the issue. A longer prompt that still packs four shots into one clip has the same problem.

options.text: It uses the word "epic". Style words are not allowed in video prompts at all.
options.explanation: Style is one of the elements Google's guide lists. The issue is the four shots in one prompt.

options.text: Teasers cannot be made with video models, so the client needs a full film crew. A real shoot day is needed.
options.explanation: The model can make teasers. The prompt just has to be planned as shots.

questions.prompt: Which is the best prompt for shot 1?

options.text: "A low tracking shot, wide, of a runner in a white sneaker sprinting on a wet street at dawn. Cool blue tones. Footsteps splash, traffic hums far away."
options.explanation: Right. It covers subject, action, camera, composition and ambiance, and it adds sound effects and ambient noise as Google's guide describes.

options.text: "Runner, shoe, street, dawn, epic, cinematic, 4k, amazing, best quality, masterpiece, trending, ultra detailed, award winning, wow. Super sharp, 10/10, wow."
options.explanation: It is a list of words. It has no action and no camera, and "amazing" adds nothing for the model.

options.text: "A runner sprints, then stops, then looks at the shoe, then jumps a fence, then waves, then the screen goes black and the logo fades in. All in one single clip."
options.explanation: This packs several actions into one shot. Shot 1 should hold one action.

options.text: "Make the best shot 1 you can, with a great mood and a great look, and make it feel like a real brand film for the launch."
options.explanation: It gives no subject, no action and no camera. The model will invent all of them.

questions.prompt: How do you make the runner say "Run your city." at the end of shot 2?

options.text: Put the spoken words in quotes, for example: the runner says, "Run your city."
options.explanation: Right. Google's Veo guide says to use quotes for specific speech.

options.text: Write "someone says the slogan" without the words, and let the model pick them.
options.explanation: The model cannot know the words. Specific speech goes in quotes.

options.text: Veo cannot make sound, so add the voice in editing and skip the prompt.
options.explanation: Veo makes audio with the video, and the guide lists dialogue cues. You may still replace audio later in editing if the client wants a recorded voice.

options.text: Write the slogan in capital letters at the very start of the prompt text.
options.explanation: Capital letters do not mark speech. Quotes do.

questions.prompt: In the second test, the sneaker in shot 2 has a red heel tab. How do you keep the product the same?

options.text: Repeat the same subject description in both prompts, and add the product photos as references.
options.explanation: Right. The Runway docs advise reusing the same product or style language across shots, and the Gemini API docs say Veo 3.1 takes up to three reference images to preserve a product's appearance.

options.text: Describe the shoe in shot 1 only. The model remembers it for shot 2 as well, by itself.
options.explanation: Each request is separate. Nothing in the docs says the model carries the look from one request to the next.

options.text: Run shot 2 again until it looks right, without changing the prompt or references.
options.explanation: Rerunning gives different results each time, but without a fix to the prompt or references you are only guessing.

options.text: Tell the client video models cannot keep a product consistent across shots, so a red tab is normal.
options.explanation: The docs describe reference images and repeated product language for this problem. Use them first.
